title: payment-api error-rate SLO burn; upstream acquirer-gateway slow
symptoms: outbound calls to a dependency approaching the client timeout
dependency health checks failing or degrading
end-to-end latency dominated by waiting on a dependency
observed_signals: retries increased request rate slightly without a user-traffic surge
caller CPU and memory stayed close to baseline
downstream_latency_ms on the caller rose toward the configured client timeout
timeout logs named a specific dependency, not the local database

timeline.event: synthetic checks to acquirer-gateway were still green
outbound p95 from payment-api toward acquirer-gateway rose
circuit breaker or retry logs referenced acquirer-gateway
acquirer-gateway recovered or was isolated; caller errors receded

contributing_factors: acquirer-gateway was degraded in one region
payment-api timeout was tight relative to the provider p99
resolution: confirmed acquirer-gateway latency on the provider status page and their dashboards
raised the client timeout only after proving the dependency was the bottleneck
enabled a circuit breaker and a cached fallback for non-critical reads
lessons_learned: distinguish caller CPU/memory (flat) from outbound latency (up)
fallback and circuit breaking should be tested, not only documented
